nodes.name: Check backend readiness
nodes.notes: GET /api/health/ready. 'Never error' + 'full response': a 503 is DATA for the next node, not a crash. If the backend doesn't answer at all, retry twice (5 s apart) before believing it, then continue with the error as data.

nodes.name: Decide: alert, recovered or quiet
nodes.notes: Remembers the last state (workflow static data) so a long outage gives ONE alert and ONE recovery, not one every 5 minutes.

nodes.name: Raise alert (fails this run)
nodes.notes: Failing on purpose: a failed run is what triggers the error workflow (WF4), which escalates to a person. The monitor cannot record this in the backend: the backend is the thing that is down.

nodes.name: Record the outage
nodes.notes: The backend is back, so now it can store what happened. Uses the 'LeadPilot backend key' credential (header x-automation-key).

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ executionId: String($execution.id), workflow: 'Health monitor', leadId: null, status: 'success', attempts: 1, maxAttempts: 1, lastError: 'Recovered: the backend was not ready for about ' + $json.minutes + ' min (' + $json.problem + ')' }) }}

nodes.name: Check: Record the outage
nodes.notes: 2xx → continue. Other answers fail the run: TEMPORARY (5xx, 408, 429) or PERMANENT (4xx, not retried).
